entries.content: She originally attended to a university where she was eager to learn and discover, running her own experiments and dissecting various animals. But this can only save her curiosity for so long. Soon, she was experimenting with dead people's bodies in order to cure death itself. Despite her extensive medical knowledge and sharp mind - she was not very popular. Her controversial and unconventional theories served to only earn her the scorn of both her fellow students and her teachers. When the opportunity to dissect the recently deceased corpse of her professor presented itself, how could she refuse? Thanks to her studies, researches and numerous experiments, she was able to revive the body of the professor, but in the place of the person there was only a soulless shell. Having killed a walking corpse and got rid of all the evidence, however, that incident left an indelible impression on her, making her feel disgusted with her own actions. However, it did not at all appease her wish to win over death itself.

One of the main mechanics that works mainly during outings in the Darkest Dungeons. As heroes traverse the darkness of the dungeons, they accumulate stress. If left untreated, high amounts of stress can mean the demise of the hero and their companions.
Stress is mainly gained by fighting during expeditions, conflicts among the heroes and some dark events. The stress bar is a gauge from 0 to 200, with a threshold at 100 stress points: once this level of stress is reached, the hero will either gain an affliction, or (small chance) will become virtuous instead. A hero with 100 or more stress must be either Virtuous or Afflicted; if something would cause their stress to exceed 100, their resolve is immediately tested.

Afflicted heroes will often hinder the mission by inflicting additional stress damage on themselves and the party, potentially dragging their comrades along in their path to madness. Virtuous heroes enjoy one of several possible combat buffs and will occasionally relieve stress of their companions and inspire them. Virtuous heroes reset their Stress level to 40-45.

Upon reaching 200 stress, a character will suffer from a heart attack and will incapacitated.

Stress can be relieved in a lot of ways: from winning a battle and completing tasks, to pleasant conversations and activities that give the characters pleasure.

STRESS between 0 and 99 points: NEUTRAL;
STRESS between 100 and 199 points: hero gains or AFFLICTION or VIRTUE and this state is locked until his stress will go down;
STRESS at 200 points: HEART ATTACK.
